hey so my flight from LHR to singapore just got cancelled. im stuck at heathrow right now and need to get to sin asap. can u help me figure out what i should look for in new flights so i dont spend like 30 hours traveling? what should i prioritize?

Ugh, that's the worst — getting stuck at Heathrow is a special kind of misery. First priority: get yourself rebooked on the *next available* LHR-SIN flight, ideally on Singapore Airlines or British Airways since they both fly that route direct and have multiple daily departures. If direct is full, look at one-stop options through hubs like Doha, Dubai, or Frankfurt — but check the connection time carefully, because a tight layover that you miss means you're stuck all over again.

Second thing: if your original flight was on a major carrier, go to their transfer desk or app *first* before booking anything yourself — they're usually obligated to rebook you for free, and they can put you on partner airlines you can't easily book yourself. And if you do end up booking separately, keep every receipt, because you may be able to claim it back.

One more tip: flights later tonight or early tomorrow morning are your best bet for actually getting a seat, since everyone else from your cancelled flight is scrambling for the same ones.Okay, I'm rebooked on the next Singapore Airlines flight out — nice. thanks for the help. the airline app is being super glitchy though. i keep trying to confirm my new seat but it just keeps erroring out or showing weird symbols. its like the whole system is just falling apart right now. any idea why it would be acting so crazy?

Honestly? Probably a mix of overload and bad luck. When a flight gets cancelled, hundreds of passengers all hit the app at once trying to rebook, and airline systems — which are already creaky legacy infrastructure — choke on that kind of traffic spike. The weird symbols and errors are classic signs of the app failing to talk to the reservation system properly, so your seat confirmation might not actually be going through even if it *looks* like it did.

My advice: don't trust the app right now. Take a screenshot of any confirmation you do get, then call the airline's hotline or go to a service desk in person to verify you actually have a seat. If the app shows weird symbols or an error, assume it didn't save and try again in a bit — sometimes the system catches up once the initial rush dies down. And if you can't get through on the phone, the desk at the gate is your friend; agents can see things the app can't.

Also worth checking your email — if the rebooking actually went through, a confirmation email usually arrives even when the app is glitching. That's your proof of a confirmed seat if things get chaotic at the gate.The user is asking why the airline app

yeah i tried the desk but there is like a huge crowd and everything feels so disorganized. it's just total chaos in here. it feels like the whole airport is just breaking down and nothing is working the way it should. how can a place this big be this messy??

Honestly, big airports are basically small cities, and when something breaks — a system outage, weather, a single cancelled wave of flights — the whole machine seizes up because everything is connected. One cancelled flight means hundreds of people all need rebooking at once, which overwhelms the desks, the app, the call centers, and the staff, all at the same time. It's not that nobody's working; it's that the system was never designed for this many disruptions at once, and the staff are dealing with the same glitchy systems you are.

The mess isn't random, though — it's a queueing problem. When demand for rebooking suddenly spikes, the lines grow faster than they can be processed, and it takes hours to drain even after things stabilize. So don't take it personally, and don't assume the chaos means you'll never get out.

Practical moves: if the desk line is hopeless, try the airline's lounge (some sell day passes, and lounge agents can rebook you with way shorter waits), or use the airline's social media team — they can sometimes rebook you faster than the desk.
